new_scholarship.name: TaiwanICDF Scholarship Program (Taiwan International Cooperation and Development Fund International Higher Education Scholarship)
new_scholarship.degree_levels: Higher education in Taiwan (specific degree levels are not itemised in the HTML programme page; they are listed in the annual Application Guidebook PDF)
new_scholarship.program_type: Development-aid scholarship from an international cooperation fund
new_scholarship.official_source: Taiwan International Cooperation and Development Fund (TaiwanICDF)
new_scholarship.description: TaiwanICDF's International Higher Education Scholarship Program awards full scholarships so that students from partner countries can study in Taiwan at universities that collaborate with the Fund through the Taiwan International Cooperation Alliance (TICA) framework. The Fund publishes the 2027 application round as 1 December 2026 to 15 March 2027 and requires every applicant to file through the TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System. The Fund states the programme supports the socio-economic growth of partner countries, cultivates talent, enhances the internationalisation of Taiwanese universities and broadens Taiwanese students' global perspective.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: 2027 scholarship cycle; applications open 1 December 2026 and close 15 March 2027
programme_detail_official.deadline_central_display: March 15, 2027 - official wording: "The 2027 TaiwanICDF Scholarship applications open from December 1, 2026 to March 15, 2027!"
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: The window is published on both the programme page and the Apply Now page, each last updated 2026/07/15. It had not opened on the verification date, so this is an upcoming cycle with a published window rather than an open one.
programme_detail_official.status_note: Application window opens 1 December 2026, about two months after the verification date.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: Not stated in the HTML pages read; the award follows the degree programme at the host university.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: The programme page states only that TaiwanICDF "offers full scholarships". Itemised benefits (tuition, stipend, airfare) appear only in the Application Guidebook PDF, which the fetch tool returned as raw PDF bytes and could not be read, so no individual funding component is claimed here.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: Official wording: "offers full scholarships to outstanding students from partner countries to pursue higher education in Taiwan"; itemised components are published only in the guidebook PDF, so coverage flags are left unconfirmed.
benefits: Full scholarship to study in Taiwan through local universities collaborating with TaiwanICDF under the Taiwan International Cooperation Alliance (TICA) framework (official wording: "offers full scholarships")
eligibility: Students from TaiwanICDF partner countries (official wording: "outstanding students from partner countries")
Detailed nationality, age and academic conditions are published in the annual Application Guidebook PDF and were not readable on the verification date
programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: Partner-country nationals; the current partner-country list is published in the Application Guidebook PDF.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Open to nationals of TaiwanICDF partner countries, i.e. applicants from outside Taiwan.
degree_levels: Higher education in Taiwan (degree levels not itemised on the HTML programme page)
programme_detail_official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Placement is with a university in Taiwan that collaborates with TaiwanICDF through the TICA framework.
programme_detail_official.application_method: Online application through the TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System; the official Apply Now page warns that failure to submit accurate and complete information means the application will not be processed.

requirements: Submit the online application within 1 December 2026 - 15 March 2027
Supply accurate and complete information; the official page states failure to do so will result in the application not being processed
programme_detail_official.english_requirement_note: Not stated on the HTML pages read; the guidebook PDF was not readable as text, so no language requirement is asserted.
selection_criteria: TaiwanICDF frames selection around "outstanding students from partner countries"; no published scoring or ranking criteria appear on the pages read
supplements_or_initiatives: Programme operated under the Taiwan International Cooperation Alliance (TICA), a platform created by TaiwanICDF with Taiwanese partner universities since 1998

new_scholarship.name: SEARCA Full Master's and PhD Scholarship Program
new_scholarship.program_type: Regional graduate scholarship run by an intergovernmental research and training centre
new_scholarship.official_source: Southeast Asian Regional Center for Graduate Study and Research in Agriculture (SEARCA)
new_scholarship.application_period: 1 September - 31 October 2026 (submission to the national Ministry of Higher Education); shortlisted applicants then submit through the SEARCA iSCHO portal 1-31 December 2026
new_scholarship.description: SEARCA's Full Master's and PhD Scholarship Program is fully funded by SEARCA for nationals of SEAMEO member countries who are regular employees of academic or research institutions or government agencies. Scholars take master's or doctoral degrees in agriculture, forestry and related sciences at SEARCA study posts in Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and the Philippines. For academic year 2027-2028 SEARCA publishes a staged timeline in which applications go first to the applicant's national Ministry of Higher Education between 1 September and 31 October 2026, then shortlisted candidates upload the same documents through the SEARCA iSCHO portal between 1 and 31 December 2026.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: Academic year 2027-2028; ministry submission 1 September - 31 October 2026, ministry endorsement 1-30 November 2026, iSCHO portal 1-31 December 2026, documentary evaluation 1-15 January 2027, interviews 15 January - 15 April 2027, results released from 31 May 2027
programme_detail_official.deadline_central_display: 31 October 2026 - SEARCA's published submission window to the applicant's national Ministry of Higher Education
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: SEARCA publishes one deadline for the first mandatory step: submission to the national Ministry of Higher Education, which closes 31 October 2026. Shortlisted candidates have a second, later deadline of 31 December 2026 through the SEARCA iSCHO portal.
programme_detail_official.status_note: The window is live on the verification date: applications must be filed with the national Ministry of Higher Education between 1 September and 31 October 2026 for academic year 2027-2028.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: Not stated as a fixed award period on the pages read; the award follows the degree programme at the chosen study post.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: SEARCA lists tuition and other school fees among the scholarship entitlements.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: Fully funded: tuition and other school fees, round-trip air ticket from the home country to the study post plus local transportation, thesis/dissertation support, book and supplies allowance, health insurance, and a stipend for food, lodging and incidental expenses.
benefits: Travel allowance: round-trip air ticket from home country to the study post and local transportation
Stipend for food, lodging and incidental expenses
eligibility: Nationals of SEAMEO member countries: Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao People's Democratic Republic, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste and Vietnam
Regular employees of academic or research institutions or government agencies
Not more than 40 years old for a master's degree and not more than 45 for a PhD at the time of application
Field of specialisation relevant to agriculture or related sciences and aligned with SEARCA thrusts

Proposed thesis research must contribute to increased farmers' income, improved food security and nutrition, greater climate resilience of agricultural systems, or empowered farmers, farmer groups and agricultural stakeholders and their institutions
programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of SEAMEO member countries; no residency condition is stated beyond being employed by an academic, research institution or government agency.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Open to non-SEARCA-host-country nationals of SEAMEO member countries, including applicants outside the Philippines.
programme_detail_official.research_requirement: A thesis or dissertation proposal is required and is assessed on relevance to SEARCA's priority thrusts; interview assesses personal motivation and leadership potential.
programme_detail_official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Study posts are restricted to SEARCA-designated institutions: Institut Pertanian Bogor, Universitas Gadjah Mada and Universitas Brawijaya (Indonesia), Kasetsart University (Thailand), Universiti Putra Malaysia (Malaysia), and University of the Philippines Los Baños (Philippines). National Taiwan University, Sejong University and Tokyo University of Agriculture are reserved for SEARCA's joint scholarship programmes.
programme_detail_official.application_method: Two-stage: the applicant first submits documents to their national Ministry of Higher Education; only candidates shortlisted and endorsed by the ministry receive access to the SEARCA iSCHO portal to upload the same requirements.
programme_detail_official.application_route: Applicant to national Ministry of Higher Education, then to SEARCA iSCHO portal (Ministry of Higher Education endorses, SEARCA awards)
requirements: Submission of the required documents in English to the national Ministry of Higher Education by 31 October 2026
Process university admission in parallel, because SEARCA states awards are granted only to applicants who also secure admission to an eligible university
A completed online application, since access to the iSCHO portal is granted only to shortlisted applicants
documents: Original or certified true copy of transcript of academic records bearing the university seal and original signature of the Registrar or Head of the University (BS transcript for MS applicants; BS and MS transcripts for PhD applicants)
Original or certified true copies of certificates of completion or diploma for every degree completed
Accomplished recommendation form from the academic adviser and the employer
Brief description of the research the applicant plans to conduct for the thesis or dissertation
Certification from a medical doctor that the applicant is in good physical and mental health condition and fit to undertake graduate studies
programme_detail_official.english_requirement: Preferred to have IELTS results of 6.0 or a TOEFL iBT result of 75, taken within two years before application as proof of English proficiency.
selection_criteria: Academic and professional background, verified from application documents
Relevance of the proposed study programme, verified from application documents
Communication (English) skills, verified from application documents and interview
Personal motivation and leadership potential, verified in the interview
award_holder_conditions: Scholarship awards are granted only to applicants who have secured admission to an eligible SEARCA study post
Applications are evaluated by SEARCA and by the applicant's Ministry of Higher Education, so the national endorsement is part of the award process
supplements_or_initiatives: Alumni network support through the Regional SEARCA Alumni Association (RSAA), with active chapters in each SEAMEO member country

official_contacts.general: Education and Collective Learning - Graduate Scholarship and Institutional Development (ECL-GSID), SEARCA, UPLB Campus, College, Los Banos, 4031 Laguna, Philippines; Tel +63 49 554-9330 to 39

programme_detail_official.description: SEARCA's Full Master's and PhD Scholarship Program is fully funded by SEARCA for nationals of SEAMEO member countries who are regular employees of academic or research institutions or government agencies. Scholars take master's or doctoral degrees in agriculture, forestry and related sciences at SEARCA study posts in Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia and the Philippines. For academic year 2027-2028 SEARCA publishes a staged timeline in which applications go first to the applicant's national Ministry of Higher Education between 1 September and 31 October 2026, then shortlisted candidates upload the same documents through the SEARCA iSCHO portal between 1 and 31 December 2026.
programme_detail_official.program_type: Regional graduate scholarship run by an intergovernmental research and training centre
programme_detail_official.coverage: Study in agriculture or related sciences at SEARCA study posts in Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia or the Philippines; SEARCA itself is headquartered on the UPLB campus in the Philippines

application_readiness_checklist: Be a national of a SEAMEO member country and hold a regular appointment at an academic, research institution or government agency
Be within the age limit: 40 for a master's, 45 for a PhD at the time of application
Pick one of the six eligible study posts and check that the programme there is on SEARCA's priority thrusts
Start university admission in parallel, because SEARCA states awards are only granted once admission is secured
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 31 October 2026 ministry submission deadline, after which the ministry will not endorse the candidate
Not being shortlisted by the ministry, which is the only route to the SEARCA iSCHO portal
Naming a study post reserved for SEARCA joint scholarship programmes such as NTU, Sejong University or Tokyo University of Agriculture
A thesis proposal that does not match the four published SEARCA outcomes
estimated_uncovered_costs: No published gap: entitlements cover fees, travel, thesis support, books, insurance and living stipend, so personal extras such as personal items remain the only likely unreimbursed cost
document_audit: Ensure transcripts are certified and bear the university seal and Registrar signature, with BS transcripts for MS applicants and BS plus MS for PhD applicants
Include both the academic adviser and employer recommendation forms
Obtain the medical fitness certification early, since it is a common late-stage blocker

alerts.message: 31 October 2026 is the only public application deadline in the SEARCA cycle; the iSCHO upload deadline of 31 December 2026 applies only to ministry-endorsed candidates.

submission_workflow: Choose a SEARCA study post and secure or start admission
Prepare documents in English, including the research proposal and medical certificate
File with the national Ministry of Higher Education before 31 October 2026
If endorsed, upload the same documents to the SEARCA iSCHO portal between 1 and 31 December 2026
Prepare for documentary evaluation and an interview, with results from 31 May 2027

institution_check_required: Confirm the intake dates and tuition arrangements of the chosen study post, since SEARCA awards only follow a university admission

Whether individual joint scholarship slots closed as "filled" affect this full scholarship (the full programme page lists them separately)

new_scholarship.name: ADB-Japan Scholarship Program (JSP)
new_scholarship.program_type: Multilateral scholarship financed by the Government of Japan and administered by the Asian Development Bank
new_scholarship.official_source: Asian Development Bank (financed by the Government of Japan)
new_scholarship.deadline: No single ADB deadline; applications go to a designated institution at least six months before the intended start of studies
new_scholarship.application_period: Rolling, institution-led: ADB instructs applicants to send applications at least six months prior to the planned commencement of studies, so a 2027 start can be applied for now
new_scholarship.description: The ADB-Japan Scholarship Program awards about 135 graduate scholarships a year for study in economics, business and management, science and technology and other development-related fields at 27 designated institutions in Asia and the Pacific, 17 of which are in Japan. The Japanese Government finances the programme and ADB administers it, including selecting awardees. Applicants apply directly to a designated institution, which screens and ranks them before ADB reviews the list and recommends awardees to the Executive Director of Japan for formal approval.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: Continuous, institution-led intake; ADB requires applications to be sent to the chosen academic institution at least six months before the intended start of studies
programme_detail_official.deadline_central_display: No central ADB deadline - ADB states applications should be sent at least six months prior to the planned time the applicant wishes to commence studies, and each designated institution sets its own intake
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: ADB publishes a rule rather than a calendar deadline, so the record is recorded as open with a recurring deadline precision. Institution-specific 2027 dates were not confirmed on ADB pages during this research.
programme_detail_official.status_note: The programme has no closed annual window: applications are accepted for future intakes and ADB asks for them at least six months before the intended start date.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: ADB lists full tuition fees among the scholarship benefits.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: Full tuition fees, monthly subsistence allowance including housing, books and instructional materials, medical insurance and travel expenses, plus a special grant for thesis preparation in special circumstances; conditional on a two-year return-to-home-country work obligation.
benefits: Monthly subsistence allowance, including housing allowance
Special grant to support thesis preparation, in special circumstances
Preparatory language and computer courses, in special circumstances
eligibility: National of an ADB borrowing member country and a Japanese ODA scholarship-eligible country; ADB publishes the list of eligible countries on the programme page
No dual citizenship of a developed country
Admission to an approved master's course at an ADB designated institution
Bachelor's degree with a superior academic record
At least two years of full-time professional work experience after completing a university degree
Proficiency in English for study at the designated institution
Not more than 35 years old at the time of application, except for nationals of certain ODA recipient countries where ADB may waive the age limit
Not an ADB staff member, management staff member or consultant, nor the relative of such a person
Not a staff member of a designated institution, or the relative of such a person
Not permanently living or working outside the applicant's home country
Not already enrolled in a graduate degree programme
programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: Citizenship of an ADB borrowing member country that is also Japanese ODA scholarship-eligible; the applicant must be living and working in the home country at the time of application.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Open to nationals of eligible ADB borrowing member countries studying outside their own country at a designated institution; most designated institutions are in Japan.
programme_detail_official.research_requirement: A special grant to support thesis preparation may be available in special circumstances.
programme_detail_official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Field of study must fall within ADB's development-related areas; 27 designated institutions host the programme across Asia and the Pacific, 17 of them in Japan.
programme_detail_official.application_method: Request information and application forms from the chosen academic institution, indicate to that institution that you are applying for admission and wish to be considered for the ADB-JSP Scholarship, and submit the institution application form together with the ADB-JSP application sheet to the institution.
programme_detail_official.application_route: Applicant to a designated academic institution, which ranks and forwards the list to ADB (ADB recommends to the Executive Director of Japan, which formally approves)
requirements: Applications must be sent to the institution at least six months before the intended start of studies
Latest income tax return or certification of annual or monthly salary, whichever is available
Accurate and complete documentation - ADB warns that an application may not be processed, or an award terminated, if information is found to be false
documents: Income tax return or salary certification
programme_detail_official.english_requirement: Proficiency in English, as required for study at the designated institution.
selection_criteria: Each academic institution screens and ranks applicants using its own selection criteria while respecting ADB's eligibility requirements and selection criteria
ADB reviews the ranked lists submitted by institutions and recommends awardees against ADB's selection criteria to the Executive Director of Japan for formal approval
award_holder_conditions: Must return to and work in the home country for at least two years after completing studies, contributing to its development
Must secure admission to a designated institution, since applications are filed with the institution
Award may be terminated if documentation or information supplied is found to be false
supplements_or_initiatives: Special grants for thesis preparation and preparatory language or computer courses are available in special circumstances
Designated academic institutions hold in-country information sessions to help applicants choose a course

official_contacts.general: Scholarships in Asia and the Pacific, Asian Development Bank (contact form on the programme page)

programme_detail_official.description: The ADB-Japan Scholarship Program awards about 135 graduate scholarships a year for study in economics, business and management, science and technology and other development-related fields at 27 designated institutions in Asia and the Pacific, 17 of which are in Japan. The Japanese Government finances the programme and ADB administers it, including selecting awardees. Applicants apply directly to a designated institution, which screens and ranks them before ADB reviews the list and recommends awardees to the Executive Director of Japan for formal approval.
programme_detail_official.program_type: Multilateral scholarship financed by the Government of Japan and administered by the Asian Development Bank
programme_detail_official.coverage: Graduate study at one of 27 designated institutions in Asia and the Pacific, 17 of them in Japan

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country is on ADB's list of eligible ODA scholarship countries
Shortlist designated institutions and their master's programmes, using institution handbooks and in-country information sessions
Check your age against the 35-year limit, noting ADB waivers for some ODA recipients
Be ready to prove at least two years of full-time professional work experience
Plan the submission at least six months before the intended start of studies
common_rejection_risks: Country not on the ADB eligible list
Applying without securing admission to a designated institution
Exceeding the 35-year age limit where no waiver applies
Incomplete or false documentation, which can stop processing or terminate the award
estimated_uncovered_costs: The two-year return-home obligation is a cost in career terms rather than cash: scholars must work in their home country for at least two years after studies
Thesis and preparatory course support are only available in special circumstances and should not be assumed
document_audit: Attach the ADB-JSP application sheet alongside the institution form, since the institution expects both
Include the latest income tax return or a salary certification, whichever is available
Add certification of family income (parent's income)

alerts.message: ADB asks for applications at least six months before the intended start of studies, so a 2027 intake needs submission roughly six months ahead, and institution intakes differ.

submission_workflow: Confirm eligibility, including country and the two-year experience rule
Request application forms from the chosen designated institution
Apply for admission and indicate that you wish to be considered for the ADB-JSP Scholarship
Send the completed forms and income documentation to the institution
Wait for institutional ranking, ADB review and formal approval by the Executive Director of Japan

programme_detail_verification.cycle_verified: Programme page and Procedures for Applying page read on 2026-10-04; ADB states about 135 awards a year with continuous institution-led intake and a six-month minimum lead time before study start. institution_check_required: Individual designated institutions must be checked for their own 2027 intake dates and internal scholarship deadlines

Whether a specific institution still hosts the programme in 2027 must be confirmed
